guide.title: East Windsor, Connecticut: Trolleys, Clockmakers and Five Villages
guide.intro: East Windsor was incorporated as a separate town out of Windsor in 1768, with the Connecticut River forming its western border — a position that made it a key transfer point for goods moving north and south. The area was settled in 1680, but the first English presence dates to 1636, when William Pynchon built a warehouse at what is still called Warehouse Point, sited at the Enfield Falls, the first major falls on the Connecticut River and the historic head of navigation. Rather than a single downtown, the town is made up of five villages — Broad Brook, Melrose, Scantic, Warehouse Point and Windsorville. Cabinetmaker Eliphalet Chapin opened his shop here in 1771, and Eli Terry, "the father of the American mass-production clock industry," was born in East Windsor in 1772. Shade tobacco became the dominant crop by the 1900s, and drying sheds still mark the landscape along Route 5.

sections.heading: Trolleys, fire trucks and a village mill
sections.body: The Connecticut Trolley Museum, run by the Connecticut Electric Railway Association since October 1940 — the nation's oldest incorporated trolley-preservation organization — operates 1.5 miles of track built on the Hartford & Springfield Street Railway Company's old Rockville branch, with restored cars, a "guest motorman" experience, and seasonal events from Easter through a holiday Winterfest light display. Sharing the site, the Connecticut Fire & Motorcoach Museum holds 16 fire apparatus and 8 motorcoaches under the Connecticut Antique Fire Apparatus Association, formed in 1968. In Broad Brook village, the historic Broad Brook Mill was once the center of local life until the bulk of the complex burned in 1986; surviving buildings still show its former scale, with Broad Brook Pond and its dam across the street.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: East Windsor is reached by car via Interstate 91, exits 44-45, and U.S. Route 5, which runs the length of the town through Warehouse Point and past Broad Brook. There is no passenger rail station in East Windsor itself; rail travelers use the Windsor Locks station on the CTrail Hartford Line, just across the Connecticut River, which stops at Springfield, Windsor Locks, Windsor, Hartford, Berlin, Meriden, Wallingford, New Haven State Street and New Haven Union Station.

faq.question: How do I get to East Windsor?
faq.answer: By car — Interstate 91 (exits 44-45) and U.S. Route 5 run through town. There is no passenger rail station in East Windsor; the nearest is Windsor Locks on the CTrail Hartford Line, across the Connecticut River.

faq.question: Is there a train to East Windsor?
faq.answer: No CTrail, Amtrak, Metro-North or Shore Line East station exists in East Windsor. The nearest stop is Windsor Locks.

faq.question: What is the Connecticut Trolley Museum?
faq.answer: A restored-trolley heritage railroad run by the Connecticut Electric Railway Association since 1940, at 58 North Road. The 2026 season runs Easter weekends through a holiday Winterfest; admission $14 adults, $12 seniors and youth, $10 children.

faq.question: What is Scantic River State Park?
faq.answer: A 784-acre park in three sections spanning Enfield, East Windsor and Somers, with the Melrose and Harrington Lot access points in East Windsor's Broad Brook section. Open daily 8 a.m. to sunset; hiking, fishing, boating and birding, no camping or alcohol.

faq.question: Is there a hotel in East Windsor?
faq.answer: Yes — the Baymont by Wyndham East Windsor Bradley Airport on Main Street, with free breakfast and about five miles from Bradley International Airport.

places.name: Connecticut Trolley Museum
places.summary: Run by the Connecticut Electric Railway Association since October 1940, the nation's oldest incorporated trolley-preservation organization. Riders travel a 1.5-mile heritage railroad built on the old Hartford & Springfield Street Railway's Rockville branch, with a "guest motorman" experience. 2026 season runs weekends April-June, Thursday-Sunday in July-August, weekends in September, plus a Pumpkin Patch Trolley and holiday Winterfest. Admission $14/$12/$10.

places.name: Connecticut Fire & Motorcoach Museum
places.summary: A collection of 16 fire apparatus and 8 motorcoaches under the Connecticut Antique Fire Apparatus Association, formed in 1968 to preserve antique fire apparatus and motorcoaches. Operates alongside the Connecticut Trolley Museum at the same site, sharing its seasonal schedule.

places.name: Scantic River State Park
places.address: Melrose access: 100 Melrose Road; Harrington Lot: 25 Broad Brook Road, Broad Brook, East Windsor, CT
places.summary: A 784-acre park in three sections spanning Enfield, East Windsor and Somers along the Scantic River, with stretches of rapids and gentler water. The East Windsor section is reached from the Melrose and Harrington Lot access points in Broad Brook. Open daily 8 a.m. to sunset; hiking, fishing, boating and birding — no camping, no alcohol, pets leashed to 7 feet.

places.name: East Windsor Historical Society Museum (Scantic Academy)
places.summary: Housed in the former East Windsor Academy, a two-story Federal-style brick building built in 1817 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1998. Originally a private academy, it later served as a parish hall and public school before becoming the historical society's museum. Open seasonally; contact the society at eastwindsorhistory@gmail.com before visiting.

places.name: Maine Fish Market Restaurant
places.address: 60 Bridge Street, Warehouse Point, East Windsor, CT 06088
places.summary: The Vamvilis family opened a retail fish market with takeout fish & chips in 1980, and has run the restaurant at this Bridge Street location since 1986. Set in one of the oldest commercial buildings in the state, dating to the 1780s, with a fresh raw-fish counter and everything cooked to order. Open Sun noon-8 p.m., Mon closed, Tue-Thu 11 a.m.-8 p.m., Fri-Sat to 9 p.m.

places.name: Sofia's Italian Restaurant
places.address: 136 Prospect Hill Road, East Windsor, CT 06088
places.summary: A family-owned Italian restaurant and pizzeria in business since 1983, serving fresh pasta, Italian dinners and pizza. Open Mon-Sat 11 a.m.-9 p.m., Sun 11 a.m.-8:30 p.m. Phone (860) 623-9477.

places.name: Jimmy Chen's Asian Cuisine & Cocktail Bar
places.address: 122 Prospect Hill Road, East Windsor, CT 06088
places.summary: An Asian restaurant and cocktail bar serving noodles, ramen and sushi. Open Mon-Thu 11 a.m.-9:15 p.m., Fri-Sat to 10 p.m., Sun noon-9:15 p.m.; call ahead to confirm Tuesday hours. Phone (860) 623-8882.

places.name: Nonna's Pizza Restaurant
places.address: 140 South Main Street, East Windsor, CT 06088
places.summary: A neighborhood pizzeria on Route 5 serving cheese and gourmet pizzas, grinders, wraps, salads and Italian dinners. Phone (860) 846-4972.

places.name: Baymont by Wyndham East Windsor Bradley Airport
places.summary: A highway-corridor hotel on Route 5 near I-91, with free breakfast, fitness center, free Wi-Fi for Wyndham Rewards members and free parking with room for large vehicles.
